question: When the angle of depression from the sun was 30°, the length of the shadow of the tree was 6sqrt{3} m. What will be the length of the shadow of the tree when the angle of depression from the sun is 60°?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The length of a shadow is directly proportional to the cotangent of the angle of elevation.

⇒ New Shadow = Old Shadow × (cot 60° ÷ cot 30°)

⇒ New Shadow = 6√3 × ((1/√3) ÷ √3)

⇒ New Shadow = 6√3 × (1/3) = 2√3

**∴ The correct answer is 2√3 m.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial angle of depression (equals angle of elevation) = 30°

Initial length of the shadow (BD) = 6√3 m

New angle of depression = 60°

**Formula Used:**

tan θ = Height ÷ Base (Shadow)

**Calculations:**

Let the height of the tree (AB) be h.

⇒ In right-angled triangle ABD:

⇒ tan 30° = AB ÷ BD = h ÷ 6√3

⇒ 1 / √3 = h ÷ 6√3

⇒ h = (6√3) ÷ √3 = 6 m

⇒ In right-angled triangle ABC:

Let the new length of the shadow (BC) be x.

⇒ tan 60° = AB ÷ BC = h ÷ x

⇒ √3 = 6 ÷ x

⇒ x = 6 ÷ √3

⇒ x = (6 × √3) ÷ 3 = 2√3 m

**∴ The correct answer is 2√3 m.**

**__Additional Information__**

Angle of Elevation and Depression

The angle of elevation is formed when looking up from a horizontal line, while the angle of depression is formed when looking down. Both angles are always equal due to alternate interior angles.

Key Trigonometric Ratios

In a right-angled triangle: tan θ = Perpendicular ÷ Base | sin θ = Perpendicular ÷ Hypotenuse | cos θ = Base ÷ Hypotenuse.

Standard Tan Values

tan 30° = 1/√3 | tan 45° = 1 | tan 60° = √3.
